name: Theory
question: Does the proposed mechanism hold, and do competing explanations predict the same result?
examples: the effect runs through a named mediator
a rival theory predicts the opposite sign
literature: King, Goldfarb & Simcoe (2021); Nosek et al. (2022); Delios et al. (2022)

name: Constructs
question: Do the results depend on how the concepts were operationalised?
examples: a ratings-based score captures the construct
the scale is valid in the study population
literature: Goldfarb & Yan (2021); Hill et al. (2021); Roth et al. (2023)

name: Design and sample
question: Do the results depend on the sample, data source, time window or design?
examples: large listed firms in one database
a cross-sectional design captures a causal process
the sample is large enough to detect the effect
literature: Antonakis et al. (2010); Baker et al. (2026); Cattaneo & Titiunik (2022)

name: Analysis
question: Do the results hold across reasonable analytical choices (models, controls, exclusions, transformations)?
examples: one model specification with a fixed set of controls
literature: Götz et al. (2026); Berchicci & King (2022); Del Giudice & Gangestad (2021); Gelman & Loken (2014)

name: Context
question: Do the results generalise to other periods, countries and settings?
literature: Delios et al. (2022); Wu et al. (2023); Dreber & Johannesson (2025)
